title: The Shocking Reason Gas Prices Can’t Come Down Anytime Soon | Rory Johnston
speaker: Rory Johnston (Commodity Context), interviewed by David Lin

macro_themes.view: Flows recovering (~14-16.5 mb/d) but still millions of barrels short and very costly; Iran losing control but not out of the woods.
Stock-and-flow: six to seven months of deficits have drained buffers; need a prolonged surplus/contango before prices fall.
Crack spreads at records due to lost Middle East and Russian supply; China is the only swing source of relief; a full US export ban is unlikely, partial restriction a coin flip.
If high fuel prices persist, central banks will keep raising rates to cool the economy.

calls.condition: As long as the war continues and Hormuz remains throttled
calls.reason: Persistent supply deficit has eaten inventories; steep backwardation shows physical tightness; need a year of surplus to normalize.
calls.quote: throttled and under threat, I see prices of crude oil uh and all products continuing to grind higher

calls.condition: Unless China loosens export quotas (bearish relief) ; a US export restriction would spike global diesel
calls.reason: 1.5-2 mb/d of diesel supply lost from Middle East and Russia; demand inelastic; prices stay high until economy slows.
calls.quote: it's more likely that the price will just kind of stay high or continue rising until the overall economy begins to slow.

notes: Host states 'Wednesday, September 30th'. HO price ~$227-228/bbl flat on expiring contract. WTI quoted 'just shy of $91' at open, ~90 later.
